record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let a_n(ω) and b_n(ω) be two independent random increasing sequences built from selector probabilities n^{-a} and n^{-b} with a, b in (0, 1) and a ≠ b. Almost surely, for every system (X, X, μ, T, S) and bounded measurable f and g, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(ω)} f · S^{b_n(ω)} g converge, in L^2 or pointwise, to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)?

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Suppose that a, b ∈ (0, 1) and a 6= b. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system (X, X , µ, T, S) and functions f, g ∈ L∞(µ) we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^an(ω) f · S^bn(ω) g = E(f|IT) · E(g|IS) where the limit is taken in L^2(µ) or pointwise.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix real numbers $a, b \in (0,1)$ with $a \neq b$. Construct two independent random increasing integer sequences as follows: on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$, let $(\xi_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(\eta_n)_{n\ge1}$ be independent families of independent Bernoulli random variables with $\mathbb{P}(\xi_n = 1) = n^{-a}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\eta_n = 1) = n^{-b}$. Let $a_1(\omega) < a_2(\omega) < \cdots$ be the increasing enumeration of $\{n : \xi_n(\omega) = 1\}$ and $b_1(\omega) < b_2(\omega) < \cdots$ be the increasing enumeration of $\{n : \eta_n(\omega) = 1\}$.

Prove or disprove: $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely, for every probability measure-preserving system $(X, \mathcal{X}, \mu, T, S)$ (where $T, S \colon X \to X$ are invertible measure-preserving transformations, not assumed to commute) and every pair of functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N (T^{a_n(\omega)} f)\cdot (S^{b_n(\omega)} g) \;=\; \mathbb{E}(f \mid \mathcal{I}_T)\cdot \mathbb{E}(g \mid \mathcal{I}_S),$$
where $\mathcal{I}_T$ and $\mathcal{I}_S$ are the $\sigma$-algebras of $T$-invariant and $S$-invariant sets respectively, and the convergence holds either in $L^2(\mu)$ or pointwise $\mu$-almost everywhere.
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along random sequences
artifact.status_search_result: This problem appears in a well-known list of open problems on multiple ergodic averages. Related work by Frantzikinakis, Lesigne, and Wierdl on random sequences and pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages addresses similar averages but not the two-independent-random-sequence joint ergodicity statement with distinct exponents in (0,1). No source verifies a resolution, so it appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including random subsequence convergence questions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems on multiple ergodic averages.

status_evidence.title: Random Sequences and Pointwise Convergence of Multiple Ergodic Averages
status_evidence.snippet: Studies pointwise convergence for averages along random sequences; deterministic and certain joint random analogues remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Related random-sequence results exist, but the precise two-independent-random-sequence problem with distinct exponents is not resolved in the literature.
